title: PE.B | Probability and Statistics
text:
This tutorial provides a brief introduction to the R programming language and the RStudio development environment. The document was designed as supplementary material for any course on Probability and Statistics.
Throughout the tutorial, examples are provided on how to use R to solve problems related to different topics related to Probability and Inferencial Statistics. The examples are accompanied by interactive exercises, allowing students to edit and run the code directly without leaving the tutorial. An internet connection is required, and execution may take a few seconds. You can also copy the code into R or RStudio.

This section contains a brief introduction to R and RStudio.

3.1 Discrete distributions
For most probability distributions, R provides four types of functions. The first letter of the function name indicates its purpose:
The appropriate distribution name is appended to this letter. For example, for the normal distribution, the four functions are dnorm(), pnorm(), qnorm(), and rnorm().

Thus, once the R name of a distribution is known, its main functions are easy to identify. For example, the binomial distribution uses dbinom(), pbinom(), qbinom(), and rbinom(), while the normal distribution uses dnorm(), pnorm(), qnorm(), and `rnorm().
